name: Golden angle in sunflower phyllotaxis
summary: The golden angle is the smaller angle obtained by dividing a full turn in the golden ratio: 360/phi^2 ≈ 137.507764 degrees, where phi=(1+sqrt(5))/2. It describes rotation between successively originating sunflower florets; visible spiral counts commonly follow consecutive Fibonacci numbers.
source_title: November 23 is Fibonacci Day! — Beaty Biodiversity Museum, University of British Columbia
caveat: This is an idealized phyllotactic angle, not a universal exact measurement: sunflower heads can depart from Fibonacci structure. The visible crossing arcs are not themselves golden or logarithmic spirals. A sampled projection gap near this catalog target is only an angular coincidence and does not establish sunflower growth mechanisms.
